variations.name: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from brines & brine co-production
variations.description: Sorbents, membranes, solvents, or electrochemical cells pull lithium selectively out of salar, geothermal, and oilfield brines in hours instead of 18-month evaporation ponds, slashing land and water footprints and unlocking dilute resources (Smackover, Upper Rhine, Salton Sea) that conventional ponds cannot economically touch.

companies.name: Lilac Solutions
companies.what: Ion-exchange ceramic bead DLE modules licensed to brine owners; demonstrated at Great Salt Lake and Lake Resources' Kachi in Argentina.
companies.signal: Series C ~$150M (2024); ~$318M total raised (Lowercarbon, T. Rowe Price, Breakthrough-adjacent investors).

companies.name: EnergyX
companies.what: LiTAS membrane/mixed DLE platform plus its own Smackover acreage; commissioned a 250 tpa lithium hydroxide demonstration plant (Project Lonestar, Texarkana TX).
companies.signal: GM-led Series B; acquired Daytona Lithium's ~35,000-acre Arkansas Smackover position for A$40M (Oct 2025); targeting 12.5 ktpa by 2028.

companies.name: Summit Nanotech
companies.what: denaLi nanotech sorbent DLE tuned for Chilean salar brines, with a data/analytics layer for sorbent performance.
companies.signal: US$25.5M round (Mar 2025; Evok, BDC Climate Tech, LG Technology Ventures, Mitsui Kinzoku); demonstration plant commissioned in northern Chile.

companies.name: Adionics
companies.what: Liquid-liquid solvent DLE (Flionex) that extracts lithium chloride with high selectivity and returns brine intact, piloted across the lithium triangle.
companies.signal: $27M Series B (2023) with SQM as strategic investor.

companies.name: Lithios
companies.what: MIT spinout doing electrochemical 'Advanced Lithium Extraction' — battery-electrode-style lithium capture that works on dilute, previously uneconomic brines.
companies.signal: $12M seed (Oct 2024; Clean Energy Ventures, TechEnergy Ventures, GS Futures + venture debt); Arkansas pilot engagements.

companies.name: ElectraLith
companies.what: Monash spinout whose DLE-R electrodialysis membrane stack goes brine-to-battery-grade lithium hydroxide in one step with minimal water and no chemical reagents.
companies.signal: Backed by Rio Tinto and IP Group since 2022; 2024 proof-of-concept produced battery-grade LiOH from salar, oilfield, and spodumene-leach feeds; raising Series A.

companies.name: Vulcan Energy Resources
companies.what: Combines geothermal power plants with adsorption DLE in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley to produce carbon-neutral lithium hydroxide for EU automakers.
companies.signal: Closed ~€2.2B Phase One 'Lionheart' financing (Dec 2025) incl. €250M EIB, ECAs, KfW equity; 24 ktpa LiOH; production targeted 2028; LiCl optimization plant running since 2024.

companies.name: Controlled Thermal Resources
companies.what: Hell's Kitchen project at California's Salton Sea co-producing geothermal power and lithium from the same brine, one of the largest US lithium resources.
companies.signal: Stellantis invested >$100M with multi-decade lithium offtake; Stage 1 ~25 ktpa LHM in development.

companies.name: Standard Lithium
companies.what: Longest-running US DLE demonstration (El Dorado, Arkansas since 2020); now developing the Smackover via the 55/45 'Smackover Lithium' JV with Equinor.
companies.signal: $225M DOE grant (2024); >$1B of export-credit-agency debt interest; FID targeted ~end-2025, first production 2028.

companies.name: International Battery Metals (IBAT)
companies.what: Containerized, relocatable modular DLE plants; switched on the first commercial modular DLE plant in North America at US Magnesium's Utah site (2024).
companies.signal: World-first modular commercial DLE deployment (Jul 2024); subsequent throughput tied to troubled host-site economics.

companies.name: Eramet
companies.what: French mining major operating Centenario (Argentina), the first large greenfield DLE plant built outside China, ramping toward 24 ktpa LCE.
companies.signal: Centenario Phase 1 inaugurated 2024 and ramping through 2025-26 — the sector's key industrial proof point.

companies.name: ExxonMobil (Mobil Lithium)
companies.what: Applying oilfield drilling and subsurface skills to Arkansas Smackover brine, re-injecting spent brine; the highest-profile oil-major entry into lithium.
companies.signal: First production targeted ~2027; stated ambition to supply ~1M EVs/yr by 2030.

variations.name: Lithium from clay and unconventional hard-rock processing
variations.description: Acid or CO2-based leaching flowsheets unlock lithium from claystone/sedimentary deposits and cut the energy and reagent intensity of spodumene conversion, adding a third supply pillar beyond brine ponds and conventional hard rock — critical because the biggest US lithium resources are clays.

companies.name: Lithium Americas
companies.what: Building Thacker Pass (Nevada), the largest western clay-lithium project, using sulfuric-acid leaching of claystone; Phase 1 is 40 ktpa battery-grade lithium carbonate.
companies.signal: $2.26B DOE loan with first $435M draw agreed Oct 2025 — US government took 5% equity warrants; GM $625M JV; production ~2028.

companies.name: ioneer
companies.what: Rhyolite Ridge (Nevada) lithium-boron project whose boron co-product subsidizes lithium costs; on-site sulfuric-acid processing.
companies.signal: Closed $996M DOE loan (Jan 2025); Sibanye-Stillwater declined the JV (Feb 2025) but financing stands; production targeted 2028.

companies.name: Century Lithium
companies.what: Angel Island (Clayton Valley, Nevada) claystone project with a long-running pilot plant validating chloride-based leaching and on-site lithium carbonate production.
companies.signal: Completed feasibility study (2024); multi-year pilot plant operation in Amargosa Valley.

companies.name: American Battery Technology Company
companies.what: Pairs Nevada claystone extraction (Tonopah Flats) with a selective leach flowsheet developed alongside its battery-recycling business.
companies.signal: Multiple DOE grants for first-of-kind claystone demonstration and commercial refinery design; Nasdaq-listed.

companies.name: Novalith
companies.what: LiCAL process leaches lithium with CO2-carbonated water instead of sulfuric acid, producing lithium carbonate directly and locking some CO2 into the product.
companies.signal: A$23M Series A (2023; Lowercarbon, CEFC); pilot plant in Sydney.

companies.name: Sigma Lithium
companies.what: 'Greentech' dense-media-separation plant in Brazil produces ~270 ktpa 'Quintuple Zero' spodumene concentrate with zero tailings dams, dry-stacking, and renewable power.
companies.signal: Producing and expanding since 2023; one of the lowest-carbon hard-rock lithium operations globally.

variations.white_space: Capital intensity ($1-3B per project) and unproven first-of-kind flowsheets restrict this to a handful of mega-projects that only advanced once DOE loans and automaker equity de-risked them; the open lane is low-capex, low-acid chemistry (CO2 or chloride leaching) that can work at smaller deposits without a billion-dollar acid plant.

variations.name: Copper extraction innovation (catalytic heap leaching, electrochemical reduction, in-situ recovery)
variations.description: Catalysts, microbes, and electrochemistry break chalcopyrite's passivation layer so copper can be leached or plated from low-grade primary sulfide ore, waste dumps, and deep orebodies without building new smelters — the main lever for closing the forecast multi-Mt copper supply gap for electrification.

companies.name: Jetti Resources
companies.what: Catalytic additive that lets standard heap leaching extract copper from chalcopyrite; deployed commercially at Capstone's Pinto Valley since 2019.
companies.signal: $100M Series D (2022) at ~$2.5B valuation (T. Rowe Price, BHP, Freeport, Mitsubishi); Capstone's PV4 study expands Jetti leaching toward 300-350 Mlb cathode.

companies.name: Ceibo
companies.what: Chilean startup whose leaching chemistry accelerates chalcopyrite oxidation using existing mine infrastructure (sulfide leaching retrofit).
companies.signal: $30M Series B (Energy Impact Partners); BHP Ventures invested 2025; on-site trials with major Chilean producers.

companies.name: Still Bright
companies.what: Vanadium redox-driven dissolution plus electrowinning that converts copper concentrate (and complex ores) to cathode without smelting, claiming near-complete recovery.
companies.signal: $18.7M seed (Jul 2025) led by Material Impact and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, with Fortescue; New Jersey pilot.

companies.name: Nuton (Rio Tinto)
companies.what: Rio Tinto's bioleaching/heap-leach venture commercializing decades of internal R&D on primary sulfides through deals with junior mine owners.
companies.signal: First copper cathode at Gunnison Copper's Johnson Camp mine (2025); AWS signed as exclusive launch customer for Nuton copper (2026).

companies.name: Taseko Mines (Florence Copper)
companies.what: First new commercial in-situ copper recovery operation in the US: sulfuric acid circulated through wells dissolves copper in place, SX/EW plant makes cathode on site with minimal surface disturbance.
companies.signal: First cathode Feb 2026; 1.5 Mlb produced in Q1 2026; projected lowest-quartile cost and among lowest-GHG copper in North America.

companies.name: Gunnison Copper
companies.what: Arizona junior (formerly Excelsior Mining) that pivoted from a slow wellfield ISR ramp to open-pit plus Nuton-powered heap leach at Johnson Camp.
companies.signal: First cathode produced under Nuton partnership (2025) after original Gunnison ISR underperformed on permeability.

companies.name: BHP
companies.what: World's largest copper producer running full-scale leaching programs at Escondida and seeding the field via BHP Ventures stakes in Jetti and Ceibo and its Think & Act biomining program.
companies.signal: Multi-decade leach expansion plans; venture positions across the catalytic-leach cohort.

companies.name: Freeport-McMoRan
companies.what: 'Leach to the last drop' initiative using additives, sensors, and heat retention to recover incremental copper from billions of tonnes of legacy stockpiles.
companies.signal: Added ~200-300 Mlb/yr of low-capex cathode, targeting ~800 Mlb/yr run-rate by 2030.

variations.white_space: Chalcopyrite passivation defeated heap leaching for 40 years; catalytic leaching now has several funded players, but direct electrochemical reduction of concentrate has essentially one startup (Still Bright) — hard electrochemistry, but the prize is replacing the world's copper smelters (and their geographic concentration in China), so credible second entrants would find capital.

variations.name: Cleaner nickel and cobalt supply (hydromet refining, low-carbon laterite processing, tailings handling)
variations.description: Hydrometallurgical flowsheets (HPAL, nitric-acid DNi, pressure leaching) and carbon-mineralizing tailings turn laterite and sulfide ores into battery-grade nickel and cobalt with lower emissions than smelting — the battleground is making western 'green' nickel cost-competitive with Indonesian HPAL.

companies.name: Lifezone Metals
companies.what: Hydromet platform that replaces smelting; developing Kabanga (Tanzania), one of the largest undeveloped high-grade nickel sulfide deposits, with an in-country Kahama refinery for Ni/Co sulfates and copper cathode.
companies.signal: NYSE-listed (LZM); 2025 feasibility/initial assessment published; took full project ownership after BHP's 2024 exit.

companies.name: Canada Nickel
companies.what: Crawford (Ontario) ultramafic nickel project whose tailings naturally absorb CO2 (in-process tailings carbonation), targeting net-zero nickel plus a NetZero Metals refinery.
companies.signal: Bankable feasibility complete; referred to Canada's Major Projects Office (Nov 2025) for accelerated permitting/financing.

companies.name: Talon Metals
companies.what: High-grade Tamarack (Minnesota) nickel-copper deposit in JV with Rio Tinto, with a DOE-grant-backed processing facility planned in North Dakota and a Tesla offtake.
companies.signal: US DOE ($114M) and DoD grants; Tesla supply agreement; permitting underway.

companies.name: Westwin Elements
companies.what: Building America's only nickel refinery effort — a carbonyl-process pilot refinery in Lawton, Oklahoma, with a full-scale plant planned.
companies.signal: Pilot refinery operating; full-scale site selection (Georgia) underway; ongoing litigation with former technology partner CVMR.

companies.name: Queensland Pacific Metals
companies.what: TECH Project (Townsville) would process New Caledonian laterite via the nitric-acid DNi process with near-zero solid residue and reagent recycle.
companies.signal: Project development paused amid the nickel price collapse; company pivoted near-term focus to gas/energy assets.

companies.name: Electra Battery Materials
companies.what: Refurbishing North America's only cobalt sulfate refinery (Temiskaming, Ontario) to feed EV precursor plants.
companies.signal: US DoD awarded $20M (2024); commissioning repeatedly delayed by financing gaps — a marker of western refining economics.

companies.name: Huayou Cobalt
companies.what: Chinese incumbent that industrialized Indonesian HPAL (Huayue; Pomalaa JV with Vale/Ford), resetting the global nickel cost curve while moving to dry-stack tailings.
companies.signal: Multiple operating HPAL trains; dominant MHP supplier to battery chains.

variations.white_space: Indonesian HPAL oversupply crashed nickel prices and froze nearly all western projects — BHP suspended Nickel West (2024) and BASF/Eramet scrapped their Sonic Bay HPAL JV — so few startups attack primary nickel processing; the opening is not new chemistry but verified low-carbon 'green premium' nickel qualifying for IRA/EU rules, plus carbon-mineralizing tailings that monetize CO2 storage alongside metal.

variations.name: Deep-sea polymetallic nodule collection
variations.description: Robotic collectors lift potato-sized nodules rich in nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese from 4-5 km abyssal plains, a potentially huge land-mining alternative that remains gated by unresolved international regulation and major ecological controversy.

companies.name: The Metals Company (TMC)
companies.what: Most advanced nodule developer (NORI/TOML areas, Clarion-Clipperton Zone); pivoted to the US permitting route after the 2025 seabed-minerals executive order.
companies.signal: World-first commercial recovery permit application under US DSHMRA (2025; NOAA hearings Jan 2026); Korea Zinc $85M strategic investment; 2022 pilot lifted ~3,000t nodules.

companies.name: Impossible Metals
companies.what: Eureka AUVs that hover and pick nodules selectively with AI vision to avoid visible fauna — a lower-impact alternative to dredge-style collectors.
companies.signal: Requested a BOEM lease sale offshore American Samoa (2025); postponed its planned 2026 CCZ test citing technology readiness.

companies.name: Loke Marine Minerals
companies.what: Norwegian developer that bought Lockheed's UK Seabed Resources licenses to mine CCZ and Norwegian shelf minerals.
companies.signal: Declared bankruptcy April 2025 after failing to raise — the clearest evidence of investor flight from the sector.

companies.name: Global Sea Mineral Resources (DEME)
companies.what: Dredging giant DEME's nodule arm; ran Patania II/III collector trials in the CCZ under an ISA exploration contract.
companies.signal: Holding pattern pending ISA mining code; technology demonstrated at depth.

companies.name: Allseas
companies.what: Offshore engineering incumbent that built and operates TMC's Hidden Gem production vessel and riser system.
companies.signal: Successful 2022 pilot collection system test; TMC shareholder and partner.

variations.white_space: Regulatory limbo (ISA stalemate vs. a contested new US permit path) plus ESG-driven investor flight (Loke bankrupt, Impossible Metals delayed, automakers pledging no deep-sea metals) leaves effectively one funded developer; openings are picks-and-shovels — selective harvesting robotics, environmental monitoring/baselining tech, and onshore nodule processing — rather than new license holders.

variations.name: Rare earth mining and novel separation/refining
variations.description: New mines plus separation technologies (accelerated solvent extraction, chromatography, ionic-clay desorption) break China's ~90% grip on separated rare earth oxides — especially heavy REEs like dysprosium and terbium — which became an acute chokepoint after China's 2025 export controls.

companies.name: MP Materials
companies.what: Operates Mountain Pass, the only US REE mine, with integrated separation and a Fort Worth magnet plant.
companies.signal: DoD became largest shareholder (2025, $400M preferred) with $110/kg NdPr price floor and 10-yr magnet offtake; $500M Apple deal.

companies.name: Lynas Rare Earths
companies.what: Largest ex-China separated REE producer (Mt Weld, Kalgoorlie, Malaysia), first to separate dysprosium/terbium outside China (2025), building a Texas plant with DoD funding.
companies.signal: Commercial Dy/Tb production 2025; Seadrift TX heavy-RE plant in development.

companies.name: Solvay
companies.what: Restarted and expanded NdPr separation at its century-old La Rochelle plant, the EU's anchor separation asset.
companies.signal: NdPr line inaugurated April 2025; targets ~30% of EU magnet REE demand by 2030.

companies.name: Energy Fuels
companies.what: Uranium miner that repurposed its White Mesa mill to separate NdPr (and pilot Dy/Tb) from monazite streams.
companies.signal: Producing separated NdPr since 2024; 2026 strategic partnership with US magnet maker Vulcan Elements.

companies.name: Ucore Rare Metals
companies.what: RapidSX column-based accelerated solvent extraction (~3x faster than mixer-settlers) for both light and heavy REE separation.
companies.signal: US DoD awards totaling $22.4M; Louisiana Strategic Metals Complex targeting first salable separated REEs H2 2026.

companies.name: ReElement Technologies
companies.what: Ligand-assisted chromatography that separates heavy and light REEs (and lithium) in modular plants instead of hundred-stage SX trains.
companies.signal: DoD investment (Sept 2025); Marion, Indiana refining campus scaling; commercial qualification with magnet makers.

companies.name: Carester (Caremag)
companies.what: French separation specialist building Lacq plant to produce ~600 tpa Dy+Tb oxides — set to be the largest western heavy-RE separator — from mixed concentrates and magnet recycling.
companies.signal: €216M from JOGMEC/Iwatani and the French state; USA Rare Earth and InfraVia each taking ~12.5% stakes (2026); production from late 2026.

companies.name: Serra Verde
companies.what: First commercial ionic-clay REE producer in the Americas (Goiás, Brazil), a heavy-RE-rich feed analogous to southern China's deposits.
companies.signal: Producing since 2024, ramping toward 5 ktpa REO.

companies.name: Aclara Resources
companies.what: Ionic-clay heavy-RE projects in Chile (Penco) and Brazil (Carina) using a water-recycling, no-blasting desorption flowsheet, with a planned US separation step.
companies.signal: TSX-listed; pilot plants run; permitting and DFS advancing 2025-26.

variations.name: Critical-material substitution (rare-earth-free magnets, cobalt-free and PGM-thrifted materials)
variations.description: Engineered materials — iron-nitride and ferrite magnets, LFP/sodium cathodes, low-platinum-group catalysts — design scarce or weaponized elements out of motors, batteries, and electrolyzers entirely, attacking demand instead of supply.

companies.name: Niron Magnetics
companies.what: Iron-nitride 'Clean Earth Magnet' — the leading high-flux rare-earth-free permanent magnet — moving from pilot line to first commercial plant in Sartell, Minnesota.
companies.signal: $214M+ raised (GM, Stellantis, Samsung, Allison, Magna); $52M DOE award plus $10M Minnesota grant for the Sartell plant.

companies.name: Materials Nexus
companies.what: UK AI materials-discovery platform that designed rare-earth-free magnet 'MagNex' in three months, now scaling synthesis with UK research institutes.
companies.signal: MagNex unveiled 2024; seed-stage with Henry Royce Institute collaboration.

companies.name: Conifer
companies.what: Ferrite-based axial-flux hub motors with 'no-tool' software-driven manufacturing, matching rare-earth motor performance for micromobility, HVAC, and industrial uses.
companies.signal: $20M seed (Apr 2025; True Ventures, MaC, MFV); track to ~75,000 motors/yr capacity.

companies.name: Proterial (ex-Hitachi Metals)
companies.what: Demonstrated ~100 kW-class ferrite-magnet EV traction motor designs, validating rare-earth-free architectures for mass-market vehicles.
companies.signal: Ferrite EV motor concept shown 2023; global magnet supplier hedging both chemistries.

companies.name: CATL
companies.what: Drove cobalt- and nickel-free LFP/LMFP to >40% of global EV battery output and launched Naxtra sodium-ion — by volume the largest critical-mineral substitution in the market.
companies.signal: World #1 cell maker; sodium-ion mass production announced 2025.

companies.name: Mattiq
companies.what: Northwestern 'megalibrary' high-throughput electrochemistry to design catalysts that slash platinum-group and iridium loadings in electrolyzers and fuel cells.
companies.signal: ~$15M Series A (2023); industrial co-development programs.

variations.white_space: Physics caps substitutes — iron nitride and ferrite give up energy product versus NdFeB, so they only address mid-performance motors — and magnet manufacturing scale-up is slow, capital-heavy, and incumbent-dominated, which is why credible players are scarce; AI-accelerated alloy discovery plus the post-2025 China export-control panic (and US price floors) create the best entry window this decade.

variations.name: Battery-grade refining and midstream chemical conversion (lithium hydroxide, HPMSM, CAM precursors, reagent regeneration)
variations.description: Electrochemical and plasma processes convert mined intermediates into battery-grade chemicals (LiOH, manganese sulfate, cathode precursors) outside China while regenerating acids and bases on-site, attacking the midstream chokepoint where China holds 60-90% of capacity.

companies.name: Mangrove Lithium
companies.what: Electrochemical cells convert lithium sulfate/chloride or carbonate into battery-grade lithium hydroxide without reagent consumption; Delta, BC plant is North America's first electrochemical lithium refinery.
companies.signal: Canada Growth Fund-led up to US$85M (2025) after $35M strategic round; plant sized for ~25,000 EVs/yr, commissioning from late 2025.

companies.name: Aepnus Technology
companies.what: Salt-splitting electrolyzers regenerate caustic soda and sulfuric acid from sodium-sulfate waste streams at lithium refineries, recyclers, and CAM plants.
companies.signal: $8M seed (2024; Clean Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon); pilots with battery-materials producers.

companies.name: 6K (6K Energy)
companies.what: UniMelt microwave-plasma reactors make cathode-active materials and other battery powders in seconds with little waste, replacing multi-day furnace chemistry.
companies.signal: $50M DOE award toward the >$200M PlusCAM plant in Jackson, Tennessee.

companies.name: Element 25
companies.what: Building the first US high-purity manganese sulfate (HPMSM) refinery in Louisiana, fed by its own Australian manganese ore.
companies.signal: GM ($85M) and Stellantis ($15M) funding; 2026: renegotiating offtake contracts with both automakers after schedule slip — project under review.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.what: Built its own Corpus Christi spodumene-to-lithium-hydroxide refinery using a sulfate-free process — the rare automaker that integrated upstream into chemical refining.
companies.signal: Refinery commissioning/first production through 2025.

companies.name: Albemarle
companies.what: One of the world's largest lithium converters (La Negra, Kemerton, Meishan, Kings Mountain plans).
companies.signal: Halted its $1.3B South Carolina mega-refinery and curtailed Kemerton trains in 2024-25 capex cuts — the defining datapoint on western conversion economics.

variations.white_space: China's scale plus the 2023-25 lithium/nickel price collapse made western conversion plants uneconomic without policy support — even Albemarle walked away — so the field thinned to electrochemical flowsheets that structurally cut reagent, energy, and waste costs (Mangrove, Aepnus) and to projects wrapped in automaker/government offtakes; price floors and Section 232-style tariffs are now creating bankable demand for whoever can finance first plants.

variations.name: Synthetic and bio-based graphite for battery anodes
variations.description: Electric furnaces, recycled carbon feeds, and even forestry biomass produce anode-grade graphite outside China — which supplies ~90%+ of anode material and imposed export controls in Dec 2024 — making this the single most concentrated battery input.

companies.name: Novonix
companies.what: All-electric continuous induction furnaces in Chattanooga producing US synthetic anode graphite with roughly 60% lower emissions than Chinese routes.
companies.signal: Conditional $754M DOE loan for second (Enterprise South) plant; Riverside plant commercial production from early 2026; binding offtakes with Stellantis (115kt) and PowerCo (32kt+).

companies.name: Anovion
companies.what: Legacy US synthetic graphite producer (New York lines) developing a $800M, 35kt anode-graphite plant in Bainbridge, Georgia.
companies.signal: $117M DOE grant; construction start slipped to 2026 amid graphite price weakness.

companies.name: Vianode
companies.what: Elkem/Hydro/Altor-backed Norwegian producer of low-emission synthetic graphite (Herøya plant) with a multi-billion-dollar large-scale plant announced for Ontario.
companies.signal: Multi-billion-dollar GM supply agreement (2024); initial CAD ~$2B Ontario investment toward 150 ktpa by ~2030.

companies.name: CarbonScape
companies.what: New Zealand company converting forestry byproducts into carbon-negative 'biographite' for anodes.
companies.signal: $18M from Stora Enso and ATL; first plant construction began Q1 2025 at Stora Enso's Sunila site in Finland, production from 2026.

companies.name: Graphjet Technology
companies.what: Malaysian palm-kernel-waste-to-graphite process, Nasdaq-listed via SPAC in 2024.
companies.signal: FY2025 10-K discloses going-concern doubt: ~$0.09M revenue, $22.5M operating loss, liabilities exceeding assets.

companies.name: Syrah Resources
companies.what: Vertically integrated natural graphite: Balama mine (Mozambique) plus the Vidalia, Louisiana active-anode-material plant — the first ex-China integrated natural graphite AAM producer.
companies.signal: Balama restarted May 2025 after a 9-month protest-driven shutdown; DOE/DFC loans plus ~$104M equity recapitalization; 67kt produced in 2025.

companies.name: Urbix
companies.what: Low-acid, modular graphite purification and anode refining in Mesa, Arizona, designed to sit downstream of any natural graphite mine.
companies.signal: Joint development agreement with SK On for anode qualification; pilot lines operating.

variations.white_space: China's Dec 2024 export controls exposed near-zero western anode capacity, yet Chinese price undercutting keeps margins brutal — Graphjet's going-concern and Syrah's force majeure are the cautionary tales; 2025 US anti-dumping duties (effective rates in the hundreds of percent) plus DOE loans finally give first-plant economics a floor, favoring whoever locks fixed-price automaker offtakes.

variations.name: Tailings and mine-waste reprocessing for metals recovery
variations.description: Hydrometallurgy, novel separation, and bio-processes re-mine the world's billions of tonnes of tailings and slag for cobalt, copper, rare earths, and nickel — supply that needs no new mine permit and remediates legacy environmental liabilities at the same time.

companies.name: Phoenix Tailings
companies.what: Recovers rare earths and other metals from mining waste and produces finished Nd/NdPr, Dy, and Tb metal at US facilities with no Chinese inputs and no hazardous waste.
companies.signal: Series B closed at $76M (2025) plus $40M strategic capital; Exeter, NH metallization plant scaling from 200t toward 1,000+t; announced go-public via Plum Acquisition III SPAC (late 2025).

companies.name: Regeneration
companies.what: RESOLVE-created enterprise that re-mines legacy sites and tailings for critical minerals and funds habitat restoration with the proceeds.
companies.signal: Rio Tinto invested $2M and screens its legacy sites for projects; Mejuri founding jewelry-sector investment.

companies.name: Jubilee Metals Group
companies.what: AIM/JSE-listed processor recovering PGMs and chrome from South African tailings at commercial scale, with copper/cobalt waste processing built in Zambia.
companies.signal: Profitable multi-year chrome/PGM tailings operations; strategic review refocusing portfolio 2025.

companies.name: Eurasian Resources Group (Metalkol RTR)
companies.what: Reprocesses historic Kolwezi (DRC) copper-cobalt tailings into one of the world's largest cobalt outputs — the at-scale proof that tailings can be tier-one supply.
companies.signal: ~20kt+ cobalt capacity operating since 2019.

companies.name: Rio Tinto
companies.what: Extracts scandium from titanium-dioxide waste streams in Quebec and lithium from 90 years of borate tailings at Boron, California under its 'full value mining' program.
companies.signal: Commercial scandium oxide production since 2021; Boron lithium demonstration.

companies.name: Cobalt Blue Holdings
companies.what: Reprocessing pyrite (waste) streams at Broken Hill for cobalt and building a planned Kwinana cobalt-nickel refinery.
companies.signal: Demonstration plant produced mixed hydroxide; progress slowed by weak cobalt prices.

variations.white_space: The barrier is legal, not technical: acquiring tailings means acquiring perpetual environmental liability, and feedstock chemistry varies dam to dam, which scares generalist capital; DoD/DOE rare-earth-from-waste funding and liability-transfer deal structures with majors (the Regeneration model) are the wedge, and failures here are scarce because so few have tried.

variations.name: AI-driven exploration, geophysics, and drilling automation
variations.description: Machine learning over geoscience data, novel sensors (muon tomography, seismic micro-arrays, drill-core scanners), and autonomous rigs find and delineate deposits under cover faster and far cheaper than the <1% industry hit rate — discovery being the longest-lead bottleneck in minerals supply.

companies.name: KoBold Metals
companies.what: Full-stack AI explorer that takes its own discoveries to development; Mingomba (Zambia) is shaping up as one of the largest high-grade copper finds in decades.
companies.signal: $537M Series C (Jan 2025) at ~$3B valuation (Bezos/Gates-backed); 60+ projects on five continents.

companies.name: Earth AI
companies.what: Pairs predictive targeting with its own low-cost drill rigs (~$100/m), verifying its AI targets by drilling them itself in Australia.
companies.signal: $20M oversubscribed round (Jan 2025); claimed ~75% drilling success rate on greenfield targets (Mo, Ni, PGE discoveries).

companies.name: Fleet Space Technologies
companies.what: ExoSphere: satellite-linked seismic node arrays plus AI for rapid 3D subsurface imaging, used by Rio Tinto, Barrick and hundreds of explorers.
companies.signal: Series D (2023) at ~A$800M valuation; hundreds of surveys delivered.

companies.name: VerAI Discoveries
companies.what: AI targeting of concealed deposits under cover where conventional geophysics struggles, building a portfolio of staked discoveries.
companies.signal: $24M Series B (Feb 2025); 60+ mineral targets/projects.

companies.name: GeologicAI
companies.what: Robotic multi-sensor drill-core scanners plus AI 'decision engineering' that re-logs core in real time for grade and recovery modeling.
companies.signal: $44M Series B (2024).

companies.name: Ideon Technologies
companies.what: Muon tomography — cosmic-ray imaging from boreholes — producing density maps of orebodies hundreds of meters underground without drilling grids.
companies.signal: ~US$16M raised (Playground Global-led); trials with major miners.

companies.name: Durin
companies.what: Building sensor-rich, increasingly autonomous exploration drill rigs to attack drilling cost — the single largest exploration expense.
companies.signal: $3.4M pre-seed (Apr 2025) led by 8090 Industries with a16z, Lux; first rig (300m capability) drilling 2025.

companies.name: Ivanhoe Electric
companies.what: Friedland-led explorer pairing proprietary Typhoon high-power geophysics with AI inversion (Computational Geosciences) to find deep US copper, advancing Santa Cruz, Arizona.
companies.signal: NYSE-listed; Santa Cruz feasibility and construction decision path 2025-26; Saudi Ma'aden JV.

variations.name: Bio-mining and phytomining
variations.description: Engineered microbes leach metals from low-grade ore and waste while hyperaccumulator plants literally farm nickel from metal-rich soils, offering near-zero-blast, low-energy metal recovery — and often stacking revenue with CO2 removal or remediation.

companies.name: Genomines
companies.what: Genetically enhanced hyperaccumulator plants that concentrate nickel from soils and tailings, processed into battery-grade product after harvest.
companies.signal: $45M Series A (Sep 2025; Engine Ventures, Forbion BioEconomy); ~$62M total including French government grants.

companies.name: Metalplant
companies.what: Nickel phytomining farms in Albania using Odontarrhena hyperaccumulators, paired with olivine spreading so each tonne of nickel also sequesters CO2.
companies.signal: Seed-stage; pilot harvests producing nickel plus carbon-removal credits.

companies.name: Endolith
companies.what: AI-monitored microbial consortia ('mining athletes') injected into copper heaps to boost chalcopyrite leach recovery; lithium biomining in development.
companies.signal: $13.5M seed (2025; Squadra-led) plus $16.5M (Nov 2025) to move from Denver lab onto operating heaps; validated in a BHP-led program.

companies.name: Cemvita
companies.what: Houston synthetic-biology company whose biomining unit seeded the field (spun into Endolith); now focused on subsurface microbes including 'gold hydrogen' and bio-manufacturing.
companies.signal: Pivoted away from copper biomining — itself a datapoint that standalone biomining needed mine-operator pull.

companies.name: BacTech Environmental
companies.what: Listed bioleaching developer applying proven arsenopyrite-oxidizing bacteria to clean up arsenic-laden concentrates while recovering metals (Ecuador project).
companies.signal: Decades-old proven tech base; Ponce Enriquez bioleach plant in development.

companies.name: Allonnia
companies.what: Ginkgo Bioworks spinout (Gates Frontier-backed) applying engineered biology to mine tailings remediation and metal recovery from waste streams.
companies.signal: Partnerships in oil-sands tailings and mining waste; venture-backed.

variations.white_space: Microbial kinetics are slow and phytomining is land- and time-hungry, so economics only close on nickel-rich ultramafic soils and on waste streams where remediation budgets or CO2-removal credits stack with metal revenue; the field is thin enough that a player proving stacked-revenue unit economics at one site could own the category.

variations.name: Low-impact and precision mining (surgical extraction, ore sorting, clean process chemistry)
variations.description: Borehole-scale 'surgical' extraction, sensor-based bulk ore sorting, and regenerated process reagents shrink the energy, waste rock, and chemical footprint per tonne of metal — making small, high-grade, or socially constrained deposits mineable at all.

companies.name: Novamera
companies.what: Surgical Mining: imaging-guided large-diameter drilling that extracts narrow high-grade veins with ~95% less waste and no open pit, sold as a service.
companies.signal: World-first commercial surgical-mining extraction at Golden Promise, Newfoundland (Nov 2025); Northstar services contract (US$1.5M advance); DIGITAL co-investments $3.5M + $4.0M; Series A underway.

companies.name: MineSense
companies.what: ShovelSense XRF sensors on shovels and belts classify ore vs. waste in real time, cutting hauling/processing of barren rock at operating copper mines (Teck Highland Valley, Copper Mountain).
companies.signal: US$42M (2022) and US$18M (2024) rounds; strategic investors include Caterpillar, ABB, Mitsubishi.

companies.name: NextOre
companies.what: CSIRO-spun magnetic resonance analyzers for bulk ore sorting on conveyors and trucks, measuring whole-stream copper grade in seconds.
companies.signal: Commercial deployments including Carmen Copper (Philippines) and trials in Chile/Australia.

companies.name: Travertine Technologies
companies.what: Electrochemical process regenerating sulfuric acid from gypsum/sulfate mine waste while mineralizing CO2 into carbonates — circular reagent chemistry for lithium, nickel, and REE extraction.
companies.signal: US$8.5M (Jun 2024) co-led by Holcim MAQER Ventures with Grantham Foundation and Clean Energy Ventures; piloting with critical-minerals projects.

variations.white_space: Mining's conservatism and first-of-kind operational risk keep adoption slow even when sensors are proven, and few startups survive the 5-10 year sales cycle; the opening is outcome-priced mining-as-a-service on stranded small/high-grade deposits (Novamera's model) and reagent circularity tied to acid supply security, both of which sidestep the 'sell tech to a skeptical miner' problem.
